result.summary: Builds follow-up performance optimizations on top of PR 36895's serialized witness stack representation in CScriptWitness. Directly deserializes witness data into raw serialized bytes without intermediate vector allocations, inlines compact size decoding for iteration, records the byte offset of the last element for O(1) access, and defers witness-to-vector conversion in script verification until program rules require it.
result.problem: Blocks packed with millions of tiny witness elements can impose excessive CPU and memory overhead during deserialization and validation. Even when witness stacks are stored in serialized form, intermediate vector conversions, non-inlined compact size parsing, O(N) traversal to find the final stack element, and eager witness-to-vector conversions for unexecuted or invalid witness programs waste substantial processing time.
evidence: Author's benchmarks show total receipt-to-accept/reject time dropping from 128ms on master (185ms minimal serialized) down to 14ms with all optimizations for synthetic blocks containing 2.0M 1-byte witness elements in unknown witness versions and bad commitments.

Author notes in commit d4f200ef35 that direct deserialization makes reading a block with millions of 1-byte elements about 10x faster, while commit 5efcd887c5 notes inlining compact size decoding makes iteration 5-7x faster.
result.scope_notes: Stacked on open PR #36895; several commits in the stack are mechanical scripted-diffs that migrate direct CScriptWitness::stack accesses across the codebase.
result.card: This draft PR implements optimization follow-ups on top of PR 36895, optimizing CScriptWitness serialization, iteration, and validation. It deserializes witness data directly into packed serialized bytes, inlines compact size parsing, caches the last item offset for O(1) back() access, and defers witness-to-vector conversion in VerifyWitnessProgram until needed. Author benchmarks demonstrate up to a 9x speedup (128ms down to 14ms) when validating synthetic blocks containing millions of minimal witness elements. The PR depends on #36895 being merged first.
uncertainties: The patch diff itself was not provided in the prompt, though commit messages and descriptions are detailed.

risk.why: A flaw in CompactSize parsing or witness deserialization and validation short-circuiting could cause consensus divergence or accept invalid blocks.
